                                                Women's World Para Ice Hockey Championship Insider | Picture Day

                                                By USA Hockey, 11/22/26, 8:30AM EST

                                                Share

                                                Follow the U.S. Women's National Sled Team at the 2026 WPIH Women's World Championship

                                                Sunday, Nov. 22 | Picture Day

                                                Listen to audio version of this article
                                                Sponsored by
                                                0:00 / 3:22
                                                Instaread

                                                The U.S. Women’s National Sled Team got to sleep in Sunday morning, making up for lost time after the previous day’s travel and time change.  

                                                After a laid-back morning settling into Newcastle, Team USA hit the ice for the first time Sunday afternoon at Hunter Ice Skating Stadium in Warners Bay. 


                                                The U.S. took a team photo, donning blue jerseys for the shot, before an hour-long practice session led by head coach Rose Misiewicz and assistant coaches Hannah DeLong and Lauren Roethlisberger. 

                                                Following practice, Team USA went back to the hotel in two passenger vans, with some still adjusting to the sensation of riding on the “wrong” side of the road, before enjoying dinner together.  

                                                OUTBACK INTEL | HOPE MAGELKY, GOALTENDER  

                                                Each day, the Insider will feature a member of the U.S. Women's National Sled Team in Outback Intel.  

                                                First up: goaltender Hope Magelky (Bismarck, N.D.). 

                                                What’s your nickname? 

                                                Magelks 

                                                How’d you pick your number? 

                                                I’m number 33. My favorite number is 3 but it’s not a goalie number so I went with 33. 

                                                Who’s your favorite music artist and what’s your favorite song by them? 

                                                Noah Kahan, Orange Juice 

                                                What’s your favorite hockey memory? 

                                                Winning gold at the World Championship last year. It was the first-ever Women’s Worlds, and being able to win that with the team was an amazing experience.  

                                                What’s your favorite thing to do off the ice?  

                                                I’m a huge birder. I love birds. I love being in Australia because there’s so many different birds here that you can’t see in the States. I’m super hyped. I’m going around with my Merlin Bird ID app trying to get as many IDs as I can.  

                                                What did you do on the flight to Australia? 

                                                It took 25 hours-ish from North Dakota. I watched some movies then conked out.  

                                                What are you thankful for? 

                                                I’m just thankful to be here with my teammates. We’re all going to celebrate Thanksgiving together. Why wouldn’t you want to celebrate with all your best friends? 

                                                Saturday, November 21 | G’Day, Newcastle

                                                The U.S. Women’s National Sled Team has officially made it to the Land Down Under. 

                                                After departing from all over the country on Thursday (Nov. 19) morning, Team USA finally arrived in Newcastle, Australia, for the 2026 Women’s World Para Ice Hockey Championship, Saturday (Nov. 21) around 2 p.m. AEDT, or 10 p.m. ET on Friday (Nov. 20) back home. By crossing over the International Date Line along the way, the team jumped a full day ahead on the calendar. 

                                                Athletes and staff took a number of different routes to Australia depending on where they started from, but most of the group met up at Los Angeles International Airport Thursday afternoon before boarding a 15-hour flight across the Pacific Ocean to Sydney. 

                                                Once the full team arrived at Sydney Airport, Team USA loaded onto a bus for the 3-hour ride north to Newcastle. The route took the team across the famous Sydney Harbour Bridge, with views of the iconic Sydney Opera House and the city’s coastal skyline on the way out of town. 

                                                The team spent the evening getting settled in and catching up on rest ahead of its first practice of the tournament tomorrow (Nov. 22) afternoon. 

                                                Team USA will take on host Australia in its opening preliminary-round contest Tuesday (Nov. 24) at 7:30 p.m. local time/3:30 a.m. ET. Every game from the tournament will livestream HERE.
